details: This package is a modified fork of the WhatsApp Baileys client library that covertly forces the linked WhatsApp account to follow specific channels and lets the operator add more channels remotely. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, two timers delayed by 90000 ms (so they fire well after startup) call a newsletter follow query for four channel identifiers hidden as base64 string literals, which decode to the JIDs 120363425000320171@newsletter, 120363420757607688@newsletter, 120363400738305381@newsletter and 120363422701490267@newsletter. All errors are swallowed, so the account owner is never shown that subscriptions were created. The same file starts an anonymous async block that waits 80000 ms, fetches hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/VinzzOfficial/VinzzNewsleter/refs/heads/main/idch[.]json, and issues a follow request for every entry in the returned JSON list (5000 ms apart). The follow list is therefore controlled at runtime by the author and can grow without any new package version. In lib/Utils/messages.js, prepareWAMessageMedia() injects an annotations.polygonVertices block and a newsletter object (newsletterJid 120363420757607688@newsletter, newsletterName "7eppeli - Information", contentType UPDATE) into every outgoing media message, silently stamping third-party channel attribution onto the user's outbound media. No environment variables, tokens or credentials are read or exfiltrated; the payload is channel-subscription steering and message attribution against the user's account. IOCs: raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/VinzzOfficial/VinzzNewsleter/refs/heads/main/idch.json; channel JIDs 120363425000320171@newsletter, 120363420757607688@newsletter, 120363400738305381@newsletter, 120363422701490267@newsletter.
